text: P01 plan: (1) h01 task: src/solve/problem.ts parses and validates a problem file per GOAL.md (every field, one line per bad field naming it, paths relative to the file's folder, folder must be in a git repo), plus src/cli/problem.ts for 'problem check' (exit 0 + summary, exit 1 + lines). Unit tests in test/solve-problem.test.ts. (2) h02: glob.ts, then P15 synthe.self.json which must pass 'problem check'. No milestone test file for P01 is on integration yet; I build to the GOAL.md contract.
P01 verdict: easy. Pure validation, no loop. One PR after the skeleton lands.

'measure draft' writes cases.jsonl, rubric.md and a dependency-free compare.js, checks both orders, prints 'agreement N/M', exits 2 under 80% naming the examples. lead: it adds one dispatch line and one help line to main.ts. h06 (judge.ts) and h08 (S01): runCommand strips SYNTHE_* from commands, so a compare.js from measure draft gets no key inside solve. Gap for lead (design choice, not built): a compare.js written by 'measure draft' cannot get a key inside solve. judge.ts runs the compare command with runCommand(problemDir, command, {stdin}) and no env, and runCommand strips every SYNTHE_* value. Options: (1) judge.ts passes only the provider key values (compareEnv in src/solve/draft.ts) to the compare command when problem.model is set; the key then reaches the person's own compare script. (2) keep keys out of commands; measure draft writes the judge as compare 'model' plus the rubric in the problem, and compare.js stays for the agreement check only (needs a GOAL-2 reading). (3) document that compare.js works only outside solve. I lean to (1), limited to compare. Tell me which and I build it after #134 lands (judge.ts is h06/h03's file).
